neighbours.label: people as individuals rather than numbers or statistics ('not just numbers', 'not a statistic', 'each is an individual')
fire: The nurse reminded us that the dead were mothers and sons, not merely statistics.
To the relief workers, the refugees were never just numbers on a chart.
Every student is an individual, the teacher insisted, and should not be treated as a test score.
We must never forget that behind each casualty figure there was a human life.
The memorial lists every name, because these victims were more than a number.
She told the patients: you are a person, not a diagnosis or a data point.
The soldiers who died were not just figures in a report; each one was somebody's child.
Poverty figures hide the fact that each of the poor is a human being, not a percentage.
quiet: The nurse reminded us that the forms were due on Monday, not merely on Friday.
To the accountants, the invoices were always just numbers on a chart.
Every chapter is a draft, the editor insisted, and should not be printed as a final version.
We must never forget that behind each mountain range there was a wide valley.
The catalogue lists every part, because these machines need more than a number of spares.
She told the students: this is a quiz, not an exam or a final grade.
The trees that fell were not just pines in a forest; each one was very old.
Rainfall figures hide the fact that each of the valleys is a dry place, not a wetland.
